reviewed_by: Claude general-purpose subagent, blind judgment reviewer (packet-only: competency text + rendered samples, no generator source), 2026-07-27 re-review batch

samples_reviewed.question_text: Compare the numbers: 307 ___ 270. Which sign is correct: >, <, or =?
Compare the numbers: 92 ___ 930. Which sign is correct: >, <, or =?

competency_fulfillment.rationale: Distinguishing even from odd requires a classification answer, but not one stem contains the words even or odd. Seeds 42, 43 and 46 key quotients (70 / 10 = 7, 10 / 2 = 5, 12 / 2 = 6) and seeds 44 and 45 key comparison signs instead.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: The 'using division by 2' mechanism is never tied to a leftover or remainder: no sample shows an odd number failing to split into two equal parts, and no sorting, true/false, or classify-this-number item of any kind is generated.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: Seed 42's 'What is 70 / 10?' introduces division by 10, outside the division-by-2 focus this competency names, and the two 3-digit comparison stems (307 versus 270, 92 versus 930) add unrelated place-value load to a Quarter 3 parity node.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: Missing are 'Is 15 even or odd?', pairing or sharing pictures, sorting a list into two boxes, and odd numbers altogether - every division sample (10 / 2, 12 / 2, 70 / 10) divides exactly, so an odd dividend never occurs.

competency_alignment.rationale: Seeds 44 and 45 are number-comparison items reused verbatim from mat_g2_na_q2_1, leaving just three even-quotient division facts, none of which asks the learner to draw a parity conclusion or builds toward one.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: Dividends stay tiny (10, 12 and 70) while the intruding comparison items reach 930; neither band is calibrated to the range of numbers a Grade 2 Quarter 3 pupil should be classifying as even or odd.
